blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Karkota Dynasty (625–855 CE) and Utpala Dynasty (855–939 CE) represent significant eras of ancient Kashmir history.
The Shah Mir Dynasty (1339–1561 CE) established the first Muslim rule in Kashmir.
Medieval control shifted sequentially from the Chak Dynasty to Mughal, Afghan (Durrani), and Sikh rules.
The Dogra Period spanned from 1846 to 1947 CE, ending with Jammu & Kashmir's Accession to India in 1947.

blocks.content: The region has been inhabited since prehistoric times. The Kashmir Valley is considered one of the oldest inhabited regions of South Asia.

items: Burzahom (near Srinagar): Neolithic site (3000 BCE); pit-dwelling culture; unique hunting scene engraved on stone — oldest astronomical record in India
Gufkral: Another Neolithic site near Tral; pottery, bone tools
Maryandal: Chalcolithic site
Kashmir mentioned as 'Kashyapmira' in Vedic literature; supposedly created by sage Kashyapa
Nilamata Purana: Ancient text giving history/geography of Kashmir Valley
Founded by Durlabhavardhana; first important ruling dynasty
Lalitaditya Muktapida (724–760 CE): Greatest ruler; defeated Arabs, Tibetans & Palas; built Martand Sun Temple (near Anantnag/Mattan); empire extended from Bengal to Central Asia
Martand Sun Temple: 8th century; greatest example of Kashmiri temple architecture; destroyed by Sikandar Shah Miri in 1400 CE
Founded by Avantivarman
Suya (engineer): Built Awantipora; diverted floods of Jhelum; famous water engineer
Shankaravarman: Expanded territory but heavy taxation
Queen Didda (980–1003 CE): Powerful ruler; initially regent for grandson; de facto ruler for decades
Rajatarangini by Kalhana (1148–1150 CE): First historical chronicle of Kashmir; 8 tarangas (books); written in Sanskrit; primary source for ancient J&K history

blocks.content: Shah Mir Dynasty (1339–1561 CE) — First Muslim Rule

items: Shah Mir: Founded first Muslim sultanate in Kashmir (1339 CE); took title 'Sultan Shamsuddin Shah'
Shahabuddin (1354–1373): Extended empire; tolerant ruler
Sikandar Shah Miri (1389–1413): Known as 'But-Shikan' (Idol Breaker); destroyed temples including Martand; forced conversions; anti-Hindu

Zain-ul-Abidin (1420–1470): 'Budshah' (Great King); golden age of Kashmir; tolerant, patron of arts & crafts; brought weaving, carpet-making from Central Asia; rebuilt temples; respected all religions
Yaqub Shah Chak: Last ruler; submitted to Akbar in 1586
Akbar annexed Kashmir in 1586 CE
Jahangir: Great lover of Kashmir; famous quote: 'Agar firdaus bar-rue zamin ast, hamin ast, hamin ast, hamin ast' (If there is paradise on earth, it is this, it is this, it is this)
Shah Jahan: Built Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh in Srinagar; Mughal gardens
Mughals built many gardens: Shalimar, Nishat, Achabal, Chashma Shahi, Pari Mahal

rows: Final Princely State Era before Accession

items: Ahmad Shah Durrani (Abdali) conquered Kashmir in 1752
Period known for extreme oppression and misrule
67 years of harsh Afghan rule; heavy taxes, atrocities
Ranjit Singh conquered Kashmir in 1819 CE
Kashmir made a province of Sikh Empire; administered by Sikh governors
Gulab Singh (Dogra chieftain) helped Sikhs; was given Jammu as feudatory
Anglo-Sikh Wars: After Ranjit Singh's death, Sikhs weakened
Treaty of Lahore (1846): After First Anglo-Sikh War, Sikhs ceded territories to British
Treaty of Amritsar (March 16, 1846): British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for Rs. 75 lakh (7.5 million rupees) — called Nankashahi rupees; Gulab Singh became first Maharaja of Jammu & Kashmir

cells: Founded Dogra rule; Treaty of Amritsar; included Ladakh, Baltistan; subdued border areas
Expanded territory; Gilgit acquired; supported British during 1857 mutiny; opened schools
Long reign; British influence strong; State Subject law introduced (1927 — actually by Hari Singh)
Last Maharaja; signed Instrument of Accession on 26 Oct 1947

items: State Subject Laws (Hereditary State Subjects Order, 1927): Enacted by Maharaja Hari Singh; defined 'state subjects'; protected land rights from outsiders — later became basis for Article 35A
Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah: 'Lion of Kashmir'; National Conference founded 1932; demanded responsible government
Quit Kashmir Movement (1946): Led by National Conference against Maharaja's rule
The Shah Mir Dynasty is frequently tested as the founder of the First Muslim Rule in Kashmir (1339 CE).
Memorize the chronological sequence of rulers: Karkota -> Utpala -> Lohara -> Shah Mir -> Chak -> Mughal -> Afghan -> Sikh -> Dogra.
Note the transition timeline: Sikh Rule ended in 1846 CE, marking the beginning of the Dogra Period (1846–1947 CE).
After Independence (Aug 15, 1947), Maharaja Hari Singh hesitated between India, Pakistan & independence
Pakistan sent tribal raiders (Kabailies) backed by Pakistani Army in October 1947
Tribal invasion started ~22 October 1947; raiders reached outskirts of Srinagar
Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947
Lord Mountbatten accepted accession on 27 October 1947
Indian Army airlifted to Srinagar on 27 October 1947 — stopped the raiders
UN ceasefire: 1 January 1949; Line of Control (LoC) established
Pakistan still occupies 'Azad Kashmir' (POK) and 'Gilgit-Baltistan'
Jawaharlal Nehru referred the matter to UN Security Council (mistake, as per many historians)
Sheikh Abdullah became Prime Minister of J&K after accession
Delhi Agreement (1952): Defined relationship between J&K and India
Sheikh Abdullah arrested in 1953; Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad became PM
Indo-Pakistan War 1965: Infiltrators launched Operation Gibraltar; full-scale war; Tashkent Agreement (1966)
1971 War: Shimla Agreement (1972): LoC converted to international-style ceasefire line
Insurgency Period (1989–2000s): Armed insurgency began 1989; thousands of Kashmiri Pandits fled the Valley (Exodus of 1990)
Kargil War (1999): Pakistan occupied strategic heights in Kargil district; Operation Vijay; India recaptured all peaks; July 26, 1999 = Kargil Vijay Diwas
Uri Attack (Sep 18, 2016): 18 soldiers killed; India conducted 'Surgical Strikes' across LoC
Pulwama Attack (Feb 14, 2019): CRPF convoy attacked; 40 jawans killed; India conducted Balakot airstrikes
Abrogation of Article 370 (August 5, 2019): Both Article 370 and 35A abrogated; J&K bifurcated into 2 UTs
October 31, 2019: J&K became UT (with legislature); Ladakh became UT (without legislature)
Delimitation Commission Report (2022): Increased assembly seats from 83 to 90; added 6 seats in Jammu, 1 in Kashmir
J&K Assembly Elections (Sept–Oct 2024): First elections after Art 370 abrogation; National Conference won majority

cells: Shah Mir founds first Muslim sultanate in Kashmir
Treaty of Amritsar; Gulab Singh becomes Maharaja
State Subject Laws enacted by Hari Singh
5 new official languages added (Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, English)
